name: Al Rajhi Banking & Investment Corp.
thesis: Index weight (raised 24-Nov from ~-0.9 pts) for risk control: trimming Jarir and Luberef would have taken the Saudi active weight to ~-9.9 pts against the 10-pt limit. Q3 profit +11.7%; HSBC Hold, SAR 70 target. 61.15 is 2% below its 50-day (62.47) and 8% below its 200-day (66.19). TASI 9,937 is 3% below its 50-day.
review: Back to -1 pt if TASI breaks below 9,800 (only if the Saudi active weight leaves room within the 10-pt limit); overweight only with TASI above its 50-day and renewed foreign buying.

name: Saudi Arabian Oil Company (Saudi Aramco)
thesis: Index weight (cut 5-Nov from +2.5 pts). Q3 adjusted net income $31.2bn (+9%), FCF $28.2bn (+20%), gearing 5.5%, base dividend $21.9bn; output 11.0m boe/d. Review trigger hit: Brent settled ~$94.6 on 4-Nov and is ~$93.9 this morning (below our $95 level) after an 8.6% one-day fall as Trump and Vance blamed the Iran war for the midterm defeat. Cash-flow quality is intact, but the oil-price support for an overweight is gone. Went ex its SAR 0.3393 Q3 dividend on 17-Nov (KWD 9.2k to cash; pay 25-Nov); 26.38 after the ex-date, level with its 200-day (26.46). Brent settled ~$93 on 17-Nov.
review: Rebuild an overweight only if Brent recovers above $100 on a renewed supply threat, or Aramco signals a dividend increase above the base; otherwise hold at index weight.

name: Saudi Telecom
thesis: OW defensive (+1.4 pts). ~5.5% yield (SAR 0.55 quarterly; Q3 record 6-Nov, paid 19-Nov, accrued late on 24-Nov), low beta, domestic utility-like earnings. 23-Nov: 40.10 (-2.0%), 5% below its 50-day (42.09), RSI 31, no company news found.
review: Cut if dividend policy changes or the Saudi underweight is closed (it is the safe Saudi holding).

name: Saudi Arabian Mining Company
thesis: Smaller UW (about -0.6 pts after a 5-Nov add). 28x P/E and beta 1.5, but the stock rose 4.1% to 57.90 on 4-Nov and would lead a Saudi rebound; we cut the underweight so a risk-on move after the oil drop does not cost us as much.
review: Back to index weight when TASI closes above its 50-day average; back to -1 pt if TASI breaks below 9,800.

name: Alinma Bank
thesis: Index weight (added 5-Nov). Cheap (~10x) Saudi bank; trend still weak (below 50-day 23.91) but now held at index weight rather than as an active bet, as part of re-deploying the Aramco proceeds within Saudi.
review: Go underweight again if TASI breaks below 9,800 or Q4 asset quality worsens.

name: Jarir Marketing Company
thesis: Overweight halved 24-Nov (~+1.5 to ~+0.75 pts). Still a top quality name (ROE 67%, yield ~6% at 15.68), but on 23-Nov Jarir said Saudi Arabia's 15% domestic minimum top-up tax (DMTT, from 1-Jan-2027; zakat counts toward the 15%) would add ~SAR 130m of tax on an illustrative SAR 1.2bn profit, ~11% of earnings; no 2026 impact (Arab News, Mubasher). The stock fell 8.0% to 15.68, below its 200-day (15.90) and 50-day (16.65), on 6.7m shares vs 2.5m average. A permanent ~11% cut to the earnings base, plus a broken trend and a stress-day beta far above its 0.4 history, justify a smaller bet; the dividend and ROE rules are not breached. SAR 0.30 Q3 dividend paid 25-Nov. 24-Nov: 15.90 (+1.4%), level with its 200-day (15.91) but not above it; SAR 0.30 Q3 dividend paid 25-Nov. 25-Nov: 15.74 (-1.0%), back under its 200-day (15.91).
review: Close the rest of the overweight if the 2027 dividend is cut or ROE falls below 50%, or if the price has not regained its 200-day (~15.9) by the 28-Dec quarterly review; rebuild only on a close back above the 200-day with the tax impact confirmed at or below ~11%.

name: Elm Co
thesis: Slight OW (trimmed 2-Nov). Q3 net profit SAR 778m, +39% y/y and 36% above the SAR 572m estimate on operating margin of 28% (23% a year ago), but revenue growth slowed to +10% and the stock is still below its 200-day average. 12-Nov close 628.00 (+1.7%), level with its 200-day (628.28); deadline 30-Nov. 15-Nov close 614.00 (-2.2%) is 2% below its 200-day (627.5). 17-Nov close 620.00 (+0.3%), 0.9% below its 200-day (625.8). 18-Nov close 612.00 (-1.3%), 2.1% below its 200-day (624.8); 7 sessions to the 30-Nov deadline. 19-Nov close 615.00 (+0.5%), 1.4% below its 200-day (624.0); four sessions to the 30-Nov deadline. 22-Nov close 595.50 (-3.2%), 4.4% below its 200-day (622.9), still above its 50-day (584.1); five sessions left to the 30-Nov test. 23-Nov close 593.00 (-0.4%), 4.7% below its 200-day (622.0), above its 50-day (583.5); four sessions to the 30-Nov test. 24-Nov: 592.00 (-0.2%), 4.7% below its 200-day (621.1); Elm said it is in scope of the 15% DMTT and is assessing the impact, no figure given (Argaam). Four sessions to the 30-Nov test. 25-Nov: 589.50 (-0.4%), 5% below its 200-day (620.2); the 30-Nov test is Monday and is very likely to send it to index weight.
review: Cut to index weight if the price has not regained the 200-day average (~SAR 636) within 4 weeks or Q4 revenue growth stays below 10%.

name: Almarai Co. Ltd.
thesis: Neutral+. Almarai: staple demand, defensive in a conflict tape. 16-Nov close 44.40 (+1.6%) is back above its 50-day (43.89) and level with its 200-day (44.46) after Sunday's 3.3% fall; P/E ~18x. The company recently published a 2026-2031 strategy presentation.
review: Review if feed-cost pressure squeezes margins in Q4 results.

name: Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Medical Services Group
thesis: Neutral+. Habib: healthcare demand is non-cyclical, ROE 31%, revenue +16%.
review: Review if revenue growth falls under 10%.

name: Etihad Etisalat Co.
thesis: Slight UW. Mobily cheap but trend broken (-12% 1M).
review: Add back to index weight once the trend recovers (above the 50-day average).

name: Saudi Basic Industries Corp
thesis: UW. SABIC revenue -35%, no earnings support; high oil raises its feedstock-linked costs on global assets.
review: Stay underweight until revenue stops falling.

name: Saudi Aramco Base Oil Co
thesis: Index weight (cut 24-Nov). Both parts of the rule met: Brent settled $89.37 on 23-Nov and Q3 crack margins softened (Q3 profit -27% q/q). 101.10 is 15% below its 50-day (119.9), RSI 25; cheap (~11x annualised 9M EPS) but no catalyst while oil falls.
review: Rebuild only if crack margins re-widen (company disclosure) with Brent back above $95.

name: BUPA Arabia
thesis: OW. Bupa: health insurance, net cash, steady.
review: Review on Q4 claims ratio.

name: ACWA Co
thesis: UW. ACWA 73x PE, high leverage, -22% 3M.
review: Stay underweight while P/E is above 40x and leverage is high.

name: Power & Water Utility Co. (Marafiq)
thesis: OFF-INDEX. Marafiq: regulated utility, strongest Saudi momentum (+24% 6M). Approved on the KFH Shariah list 2Q-2026. 22-Nov: 43.68 (-5.0%, no company news found), still 15% above its 200-day (37.9).
review: Cut if price closes below the 200-day average.

name: Nahdi Medical Co.
thesis: OFF-INDEX. Nahdi: pharmacy chain, 6.1% yield, ROE 30%, defensive. Approved on the KFH Shariah list 2Q-2026. 24-Nov: 89.40 (-2.1%) after Nahdi said new utility tariffs from 1-Jan-2027 lift operating costs by ~0.5% of revenue from Q1-27 (preliminary, Argaam); dividend rule not breached. 25-Nov: 87.65 (-2.0%), 9% below its 200-day (96.1), second fall after the tariff disclosure; dividend rule intact.
review: Exit if the dividend is cut.

name: SAL Saudi Logistics Services
thesis: OW (bought 12-Nov from the watchlist). Air-cargo handler: Q3-26 revenue +37.5% to SAR 579m, net profit +28% to SAR 232m (9M +17%, EPS SAR 7.25) with no one-offs found; ~17x trailing P/E, ROE ~46%, yield ~4.5%, beta ~0.8. Entry rule met: 11-Nov close 167.80 (+2.8%) above its 50-day (164.61), level with its 200-day (168.33). Domestic, non-oil growth that also cuts the Saudi underweight by ~1 pt and puts idle cash to work. Not yet in the factor model; scored at the quarterly review. 12-Nov close 169.70 (+1.1%) is above its 50-day (164.6) and 200-day (168.3). 9M profit +16.9% to SAR 580m on revenue +28.2% (Asharq Al-Awsat). The US Mission's 13-Nov alert says Riyadh airport runs a limited schedule; no cargo disruption reported. 22-Nov: 166.50 (-2.9%), 1.1% above its 50-day (164.7), 1% below its 200-day (168.1); two-week check 26-Nov. 23-Nov: 165.00 (-0.9%), just 0.2% above its 50-day (164.6); two-week check 26-Nov. SAR 2.17 Q3 dividend (record 9-Nov) predates our 12-Nov purchase, so not ours. 24-Nov: 166.70 (+1.0%), 1.3% above its 50-day (164.6); SAR 2.17 Q3 dividend paid 24-Nov (not ours). Two-week check 26-Nov. 25-Nov: 164.50 (-1.3%), just 0.04% above its 50-day (164.44): the two-week check (26-Nov) passes by a hair. From here the review is on fundamentals (Q4 growth vs ~12%, airport disruption), not the entry stop.
review: Cut to index weight if a confirmed airport disruption cuts cargo volumes or Q4 profit growth falls below ~12%; the two-week 50-day stop has expired (passed 26-Nov).

name: International Holding Company PJSC
thesis: Max UW. 22x PE, zero dividend, 13% of index; poor trend (RSI 25). Biggest single active bet.
review: Close the underweight only if it starts paying a dividend or the P/E falls below 15x.

name: Emirates Telecommunications Group
thesis: Small OW (reduced 4-Nov). 9M-26 reported profit AED 17.2bn (+46%) includes a ~AED 8.0bn one-off gain on the Vodafone stake sale; adjusted 9M profit is AED 9.2bn (EPS AED 1.06), so on annualised adjusted EPS (~AED 1.41) the P/E is ~14.7x, not the ~9x we bought on. Quality intact: Q3 revenue +6.9%, EBITDA margin 46.1%, 254.8m subscribers (+29%), price above its 200-day average.
review: Back to index weight if adjusted Q4 profit falls y/y or price closes below the 200-day average (~AED 20.0); rebuild only if the P/E on adjusted earnings falls under 13x.

name: Emaar Properties
thesis: Slight OW. ~5.6x P/E; AED 0.50 special dividend went ex on 13-Nov (booked KWD 15.8k to cash); price 12.30 after the ex-date, level with its 200-day (12.29). AED 15 cash offer for the Emaar Development minority runs to 10-Dec; Emaar says it has the resources to pay in cash.
review: Add if the Fed stops hiking; cut if Dubai sales slow in Q4 or a buyout is priced at a premium that needs debt beyond ~1x EBITDA.

name: Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank
thesis: Overweight raised 26-Nov to ~+1.8 pts with the DIB proceeds: keeps the UAE Islamic-bank exposure while swapping DIB's undisclosed, share-funded merger for a clean story. ROE ~26%; Morgan Stanley moved UAE equities to overweight and named ADIB among preferred banks (The National, 23-Nov). 25-Nov: 25.04 (+1.8%), 10% above its 50-day (22.68) and 13% above its 200-day (22.24), RSI 67. The AED 1.75bn rights issue at 16.45 is done. Approved (PASS) on the KFH Shariah list.
review: Back to +0.6 pts if it closes below its 50-day (~22.7) or Q4 asset quality weakens; the rights shares are not in our fixed-share benchmark, so judge it on price vs the index slice.

name: ALDAR Properties
thesis: Slight UW. 7x PE but beta 1.7.
review: Revisit after the February 2027 guidance update.

name: Dubai Electricity and Water Authority PJSC
thesis: Overweight raised 24-Nov to ~+1.2 pts with the ADNOC Drilling proceeds: regulated utility, ~4.6% yield, beta 0.6; 2.87 is above its 50-day (2.72) and 200-day (2.76), RSI 68. Replaces oil-services beta with defensive, non-oil UAE earnings while keeping the UAE neutral.
review: Review if tariffs or the dividend policy change; trim back to +0.4 pts if price closes below the 200-day (~2.76).

name: ADNOC Gas
thesis: Neutral. 5.6% yield; gas earnings less oil-levered, EPS -20%.
review: Hold at index weight; review on the Q4 dividend.

name: Dubai Islamic Bank
thesis: Index weight (cut 26-Nov from ~+1.2 pts). On 25-Nov DIB's board approved buying 100% of Emirates Islamic from Emirates NBD in an all-share deal: 3,486,284,330 new DIB shares (0.642 per Emirates Islamic share), taking the share count from ~7.24bn to ~10.73bn and giving ENBD 32.5% of DIB (Edge Consultancy, citing the DFM filing). Combined assets ~AED 585bn vs DIB's AED 427bn (The National). No valuation, EPS or book-value impact was disclosed. On the only figures given, existing holders keep 67.5% of a bank to which DIB brings ~73% of the assets, so the deal is share-funded and likely dilutive per share unless Emirates Islamic earns well above DIB on its assets; that meets our pre-set cut rule. DIB closed 8.92 (+1.6%) on 3x average volume, RSI 86, 18% above its 200-day (7.55): the market is pricing the deal favourably before any terms. Sold 161,300 at 8.92 (bought at 8.56 on 23-Nov). Needs a General Assembly, CBUAE and CMA approval; no completion date.
review: Rebuild an overweight only if the circular shows EPS and book value per share accretive for DIB holders and the price is back nearer its 200-day; go below index weight if the GA circular shows clear dilution. The new shares will not be in our fixed-share benchmark: judge on price vs the index slice.

name: Emirates Integrated Telecommunications Company
thesis: OW. du: +28% YTD, 5.3% yield, beta 0.26; defensive momentum.
review: Cut if price closes below the 200-day average.

name: ADNOC Drilling Company PJSC
thesis: Index weight (cut 24-Nov from ~+0.8 pts). Review rule hit: Brent settled $89.37 on 23-Nov (-3.5%, lowest since 28-Aug) as Libya's Sharara line reopened and the IEA sees a ~2m b/d Q4 surplus. 35% ROE and above its 200-day (5.71 vs 5.65), but the oil-price support for an overweight is gone.
review: Rebuild an overweight only if Brent settles back above $95 with rig-count guidance intact; go underweight if rig activity guidance is lowered.

name: ADNOC Logistics and Services PLC
thesis: Overweight halved 24-Nov (~+1.6 to ~+0.75 pts): sold 134,000 at the 23-Nov ADX close (7.37) after Gulf VLCC rates were confirmed down 25-64% from the October peak (Baltic/Reuters, Kpler, AJOT, Argus). EPS +103%, ~9x P/E. The residual overweight pays for continuing attacks: the strait is described as effectively closed to commercial traffic (Straits brief 23-Nov) and Trump says blockade runners will be sunk. 7.37 is above its 50-day (7.14) and 19% above its 200-day (6.19). 25-Nov: 7.65 (+2.4%), RSI 70, as UKMTO reported three vessels struck in or near Hormuz; blockade unchanged, so the residual overweight stays.
review: Close the rest of the overweight on blockade relief or a signed deal; cut to index weight if price closes below the 200-day average (~6.19).

name: National Marine Dredging Company
thesis: Trimmed 3-Nov to a small overweight. Still cheap (~7x annualised 9M EPS of AED 2.68) and above its 200-day average, but Q3 net profit fell 24% y/y to AED 768m (9M -14%, net margin 11.1% vs 13.5%) and backlog shrank to AED 51.3bn at 30-Sep from AED 56.1bn at 30-Jun (AED 54.1bn with October awards).
review: Exit to index weight if Q4 backlog falls further or price closes below the 200-day average (~AED 21.9); rebuild only if backlog returns above AED 56bn.

name: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company For Distribution Pjsc
thesis: Slight OW. Fuel retail, 5.5% yield, ROE >100%.
review: Review if fuel margins or the dividend change.

name: Talabat Holding Plc
thesis: OW. ROE 87%, 5.6% yield, low beta, +22% 6M.
review: Cut if order growth slows or price closes below the 200-day average.

name: Americana Restaurants International PLC
thesis: Slight OW. +45% YTD, ROE 69%.
review: Cut if price closes below the 200-day average.

name: Agility Global Plc
thesis: Slight OW. EPS +148%, low beta.
review: Review on Q4 results.

name: AD Ports Group
thesis: OFF-INDEX, cut 5-Nov for liquidity. Trade-rerouting beneficiary, ~21% above its 200-day average (5.07), but 30-day volume has dried up: the full position needed ~10 days to sell. Size set by liquidity: trimmed again 18-Nov to 4.5 days (110,500 shares) after 30-day volume fell to ~98k shares/day; 6.14 is 20% above its 200-day (5.12). Approved on the KFH Shariah list 2Q-2026.
review: Keep days-to-sell under 5 (resize weekly); cut if price closes below the 200-day average or shipping lanes normalise.

name: TECOM Group
thesis: OFF-INDEX, trimmed again 15-Nov for liquidity: 30-day volume fell to ~187k shares/day, pushing days-to-sell to 5.2 (limit 5); cut to 4.5 days (210,300 shares). ~7.8x P/E, ~5.5% yield, ROE 29%; 3.41 is level with its 200-day (3.41). Approved on the KFH Shariah list 2Q-2026. 20-Nov: 3.30 (-3.5%), below its 200-day (3.40); 3.9 days to sell at the 22-Nov refresh.
review: Keep days-to-sell under 5; review if occupancy falls.

name: Qatar Islamic Bank
thesis: OW. Above-trend Islamic bank, revenue +22%, Qatar holding up best in GCC. 24-Nov: 22.15 (+1.5%), back above its 200-day (22.00).
review: Cut to index weight if a Hormuz incident halts LNG traffic.

name: Ooredoo
thesis: OW. 10.6x PE, 6.3% yield, positive 1M.
review: Review if the dividend is cut.

name: Qatar Fuel Company (Woqod)
thesis: OW. Woqod: fuel distribution, 7.1% yield, +11% 1M.
review: Review if the dividend is cut.

name: Vodafone Qatar
thesis: OW. Telecom, positive momentum, EPS +24%.
review: Cut if price closes below the 200-day average.

name: Qatar International Islam
thesis: OW. QIIB: positive momentum (RSI 63), 4.9% yield.
review: Cut to index weight if a Hormuz incident halts LNG traffic.

name: Nebras Energy
thesis: OW. Nebras utility, 0.9x PB, 5.5% yield.
review: Review on Q4 results.

name: Qatar Navigation
thesis: Slight OW. Milaha: 0.6x PB, shipping exposure. 24-Nov: 10.20 (flat), just under its 200-day (10.27); tanker rates have fallen but UKMTO still reports ships hit near Hormuz, so the disruption has not eased. 25-Nov: 10.15 (-0.5%), below its 200-day (10.27); attacks increased this week, so the 'disruption eases' rule has not fired.
review: Take profit as shipping disruption eases.

name: Barwa Real Estate
thesis: OW. Barwa: 0.4x PB, 8.4% yield, +7.7% 1M.
review: Review if rate hikes continue past December.

name: Kuwait Finance House
thesis: OW (raised 4-Nov to ~+1.5 pts). Lowest-beta large GCC bank (0.21); 9M-26 profit KD 523m (+6.2%), cost-to-income 30.8% vs 33.9%. Domestic, non-oil earnings: funds the overweight while US-Iran diplomacy and a Democratic House put pressure on our oil-linked bets. 750 fils, ~2% below its 50- and 200-day averages. 18-Nov: 765 fils (-0.3%) after Iran fired drones at Ali Al-Salem air base in Kuwait (intercepted, no damage reported), its first strike on Kuwait since September; a tail risk noted, not a thesis change.
review: Review if 2026 profit growth falls below 5% or cost-to-income stops improving; trim back to +0.5 pts if price closes below ~730 fils (5% under the 200-day average).

name: Mobile Telecommunications Company
thesis: OW. 7.4x PE, 7.3% yield, beta 0.10, EPS +36%.
review: Review if the dividend is cut.

name: Boubyan Bank
thesis: Neutral. 32x PE caps upside.
review: Hold below index weight while P/E is above 30x.

name: Humansoft Holding
thesis: OFF-INDEX. 8.6x PE, 12% yield, net cash. Approved on the KFH Shariah list 2Q-2026.
review: Exit if enrolment falls.

name: Masraf Al Rayan
thesis: Index weight (bought 16-Nov with Nakilat proceeds). Qatar's second-largest Islamic bank and our largest Qatar underweight after Industries Qatar (index ~0.55%, not held). Bought to index weight to replace shipping exposure that the Shariah list removed with domestic bank exposure, and to remove a stock-level underweight that cost us on Qatar rally days (it rose 1.3% on 12-Nov). 1.979 (-2.3% Sunday) is 6% above its 50-day (1.866), 4% below its 200-day (2.071); trailing P/E ~18.7x (TradingView). Not yet in the factor model; scored at the quarterly review.
review: Index-weight holding, not an active bet. Review at the quarterly re-score; go below index weight if Q4 asset quality or margins weaken.

name: Dukhan Bank
thesis: Index weight (bought 16-Nov with Nakilat proceeds). Islamic bank (index ~0.26%, not held); 3.317 (-1.9% Sunday) is 6% above its 50-day (3.116), 1% below its 200-day (3.351); trailing P/E ~12.9x (TradingView). Same purpose as Masraf Al Rayan: keep Qatar exposure through domestic banks after the mandate exit from Nakilat, and close a stock-level underweight. Not yet in the factor model.
review: Index-weight holding, not an active bet. Review at the quarterly re-score.
